deal_summary: The visible trajectory is a labeling-equipment inquiry for vacuum-packed sausage. The initial specification called for a circular label around the sausage and a top label; the buyer later said to keep to the vacuum-packaged product, while the exact application and dimensions remained under clarification. After receiving a proposal, she said another, more compact and cheaper solution fit better. The seller offered a shorter conveyor and was still requesting the buyer's dimensions or maximum length at the last visible event. No final decision is established. [E0, E9, E14, E16]

customer_need.summary: Initially described in a date-only manager worklog as automatic application of one circular and one top self-adhesive label to vacuum-packed sausage, at 500–1,000 units/hour. In direct messages, the buyer removed the circular sausage-label requirement; the remaining packaging/application details and acceptable machine length were not fully resolved in the visible record. [E0, E9, E16]

deal_dynamics.early: A manager worklog said the customer was labeling by hand, wanted installation by October, and was not deterred by an initial 4.5M price; these are manager-recorded claims. The buyer repeatedly promised product photos, citing the weekend and a production inspection, and sent images on August 28. [E0, E1, E2, E3, E5, E6]
deal_dynamics.middle: The seller asked about label placement and whether circumferential labeling was still required. On September 4 the buyer said they would stick with the vacuum-packaged product. Manager worklogs report that an external supplier, Inox, was being consulted and then declined the requested solution; these are not buyer-confirmed facts. A proposal was sent September 9. [E6, E7, E8, E9, E10, E11]
deal_dynamics.late: The buyer reviewed the proposal, then directly said another option fit better because it was cheaper and more compact. The seller offered a shorter conveyor and asked for dimensions; the buyer said she would provide them, and a September 18 seller message again requested the dimensions or a maximum length. The revised configuration and buyer response are not visible. [E12, E14, E15, E16]

The seller offered a shorter conveyor, but the needed dimensions or maximum length were still being requested at the visible endpoint, so the trajectory remained dependent on a fit-and-price revision. The initial manager note that 4.5M had not deterred the buyer does not override the later direct price comparison, and the Inox refusal is only a manager-worklog claim. This explains the visible next-step dependency, not a final deal result. [E0, E8, E9, E14, E15, E16]
